items.en: because I am sick / in pain

bg-14-01.hint: I was tired, so I slept early.
bg-14-01.why: 피곤하다 becomes 피곤해서, and past tense is marked only on the final verb 잤어요.

bg-14-01.q: Write one sentence saying you rested at home because you were tired. Use 피곤하다 + -아/어서 and 쉬다 in the past tense (-았/었어요).
bg-14-01.why: Attach -해서 to 피곤하- without past tense, and put past tense on the final verb 쉬었어요.

steps.en: Because I was tired, I slept early.
Because I was so tired yesterday, I slept early.

ko: 어제는 회사 일이 많아서 정말 바빴어요.
몸이 많이 피곤해서 아홉 시에 일찍 잤어요.
en: Yesterday I had a lot of work at the office, so I was really busy.
In the evening, I came back home and ate dinner.
Because I was very tired, I went to sleep early at nine o'clock.

bg-14-01.q: Why was the speaker so busy yesterday?
options: There was a lot of work at the office
bg-14-01.why: The passage says '회사 일이 많아서 정말 바빴어요' (There was a lot of office work, so I was really busy).

bg-14-01.q: Why did the speaker go to bed at nine o'clock?
bg-14-01.why: The passage states '몸이 많이 피곤해서 아홉 시에 일찍 잤어요' (Because I was very tired, I slept early at nine).

items: I can link a natural cause and result using -아/어서
I can keep past tense off the -아/어서 clause and place it only on the final verb

bg-14-02.hint: Since the weather is nice, let's take a walk.
bg-14-02.why: 좋다 has a batchim, so it attaches -으니까: 좋으니까.

bg-14-02.q: Suggest going inside because it is cold outside. Use 춥다 (ㅂ irregular) + -(으)니까 and 들어가다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-14-02.why: 춥다 (ㅂ irregular) becomes 추우니까 when giving a reason for a suggestion.

bg-14-02.hint: 춥다 is a ㅂ irregular adjective: ㅂ changes to 우 before -(으)니까.
bg-14-02.why: 춥다 drops ㅂ and becomes 추우- before -니까: 추우니까.

steps.en: Since the weather is nice, let's walk in the park.
Since the weather is nice today, let's walk in the park.

ko: 숙제를 다 끝냈으니까 이제 시간이 있어요.
밖이 시원하니까 친구와 자전거를 타러 갈 거예요.
en: It is five o'clock in the afternoon right now.
Since I finished all my homework, I have free time now.
Since it is cool outside, I am going to ride a bike with my friend.

bg-14-02.q: Why does the speaker have free time now?
options: Because they finished all their homework
Because it is a national holiday
bg-14-02.why: The passage says '숙제를 다 끝냈으니까 이제 시간이 있어요' (Since I finished all my homework, I have time now).

bg-14-02.q: What is the speaker going to do with their friend?
bg-14-02.why: The passage says '친구와 자전거를 타러 갈 거예요' (I will go ride a bike with my friend).

items: I can attach -니까 after vowels and -으니까 after consonants
I can state a personal judgment or past-tense basis using -(으)니까

bg-14-03.hint: Since it is raining, please use an umbrella.
bg-14-03.why: Before the polite command 쓰세요, use 오니까 instead of 와서.

bg-14-03.q: Tell someone to close the window because it is cold outside. Use 춥다 (ㅂ irregular) + -(으)니까 and 닫다 + -(으)세요.
bg-14-03.why: Imperative sentences ending in -(으)세요 require -(으)니까 for the reason clause.

steps.en: Since it is raining, please use an umbrella.
Since it is raining outside, please use an umbrella.

ko: 오늘 오후에는 비가 많이 올 거예요.
비가 오니까 외출할 때 큰 우산을 꼭 챙기세요.
en: It will rain a lot this afternoon.
Since it will rain, please be sure to bring a big umbrella when going out.
And since the road is slippery, please walk slowly.

bg-14-03.q: What should you bring when going out this afternoon?
bg-14-03.why: The passage says '비가 오니까 외출할 때 큰 우산을 꼭 챙기세요' (Please bring a big umbrella when going out).

bg-14-03.q: Why does the passage advise walking slowly?
options: Because it is dark at night
bg-14-03.why: The passage says '길이 미끄러우니까 천천히 걸으세요' (Since the road is slippery, please walk slowly).

items: I can use -(으)니까 instead of -아/어서 before commands and suggestions
I can recognize -기 때문에 for stating reasons in formal contexts

bg-14-04.hint: It is really nice to meet you.
bg-14-04.why: Social greetings like 반가워요 always pair with -아/어서: 만나서 반가워요.

bg-14-04.q: Politely apologize for being late to an appointment. Use 늦다 + -아/어서 and 죄송하다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-14-04.why: Apologies with 죄송해요 or 미안해요 always take -아/어서, never -(으)니까.

bg-14-04.hint: Expressions of gratitude (고마워요 / 감사합니다) must use -아/어서, not -(으)니까.
bg-14-04.why: Thanking someone requires -아/어서: 들어 주다 → 들어 줘서 고마워요.

steps.en: Thank you for helping with my homework.
Thank you for helping with my difficult homework.

ko: 오늘 아침에는 버스가 늦게 와서 약속 시간에 조금 늦었어요.
친구가 웃으면서 괜찮다고 말해 줘서 정말 고마웠어요.
en: This morning the bus came late, so I was a bit late for the appointment.
As soon as I met my friend, I said I was sorry for being late.
I was really thankful that my friend smiled and said it was okay.

bg-14-04.q: Why was the speaker late for the appointment?
options: Because they forgot the meeting place
bg-14-04.why: The passage says '버스가 늦게 와서 약속 시간에 조금 늦었어요' (The bus came late, so I was a bit late).

bg-14-04.q: Why did the speaker feel thankful to their friend?
options: The friend smiled and said it was okay
The friend bought an expensive gift
The friend lent them an umbrella
bg-14-04.why: The passage states '친구가 웃으면서 괜찮다고 말해 줘서 정말 고마웠어요' (My friend smiled and said it was okay, so I was really thankful).

items: I can use -아/어서 naturally in greetings, apologies, and expressions of thanks
I can switch between -아/어서 and -(으)니까 depending on whether the sentence is a greeting or a suggestion
